title: Sarajevo, Mostar and the Bay of Kotor in Hostel Beds
subRegion: Sarajevo, the Neretva valley and the Bay of Kotor

bestPeriod.window: May to June and September to October
bestPeriod.avoid: July and August, when Mostar passes 38 °C and cruise ships fill Kotor
bestPeriod.raw: May to June, September to October

accommodation.note: Dorm beds from €15 a night, six nights

transport.note: Train to Mostar, bus to Kotor, city buses

activities.note: Tunnel museum, Blagaj and Kravica day, Kotor walls

profile.difficultyNote: 2/5, city walking and one 1,350 step climb above Kotor

gatewayAirport: SJJ Sarajevo, 30 min to the old town by bus; TIV Tivat or DBV Dubrovnik for the way home
summary: Three of the best value old towns in Europe, joined by one of its most beautiful train rides. The week starts in Sarajevo, where Ottoman lanes meet Austro-Hungarian avenues, rides the Neretva canyon line to Mostar and its rebuilt Stari Most, then crosses to Montenegro for the walled town of Kotor at the head of its fjord-like bay. Every night is a social hostel with a dorm bed under €20.
hook: Three old towns, one canyon train and six nights in dorms for under €150.

itinerary.title: Sarajevo, the old bazaar
itinerary.morning: Bus 200 from the airport to the centre takes about 30 minutes. Drop your bag and walk Baščaršija, the copper-smiths' lanes and the Sebilj fountain.
itinerary.afternoon: Free walking tour from the Eternal Flame, about two and a half hours, tips only. It covers the Latin Bridge and the 1914 assassination corner.
itinerary.evening: Ćevapi at a buregdžinica for about €6, then the view over the city from the Yellow Fortress at sunset.

itinerary.title: Sarajevo, the siege and the hills
itinerary.morning: Tram and bus to the Tunnel of Hope museum, the 800 m lifeline under the airport runway during the siege. Entry about €10.
itinerary.afternoon: The War Childhood Museum, small and unforgettable, then the cable car up Trebević to the abandoned 1984 Olympic bobsleigh track.
itinerary.evening: Coffee the Bosnian way in a džezva, then a bar crawl in the hostel quarter.

itinerary.title: The Neretva canyon train to Mostar
itinerary.morning: The 07:15 train to Mostar takes about two hours through the Neretva canyon, the most scenic line in the Balkans. Tickets about €10 at the station.
itinerary.afternoon: Walk the old town to Stari Most and watch the divers, who jump 21 m into the river once the hat has collected enough.
itinerary.evening: Sunset from the Kriva Ćuprija, the small crooked bridge, and dinner on a terrace over the river.
itinerary.sleep: Hostel in the old town of Mostar

itinerary.title: Blagaj, Počitelj and the Kravica falls
itinerary.morning: Hostels run a shared minibus day for about €35. First stop the Blagaj Tekke, a dervish house under a cliff at the source of the Buna.
itinerary.afternoon: The stone village of Počitelj, then a swim under the Kravica waterfalls, warm enough from late May.
itinerary.evening: Back in Mostar for grilled trout and the evening light on the bridge.
itinerary.sleep: Hostel in the old town of Mostar

itinerary.title: Over the mountains to Kotor
itinerary.morning: The morning bus to Kotor takes five to six hours through Trebinje and Herceg Novi, about €25. Sit on the right for the bay.
itinerary.afternoon: Arrive in Kotor, drop your bag and get lost in the marble lanes of the walled town.
itinerary.evening: Sunset drink on the walls by the Sea Gate, then burek from the bakery by the North Gate.

itinerary.title: The walls of Kotor and Perast
itinerary.morning: Climb the Fortifications of Kotor early, 1,350 steps and 260 m to San Giovanni, about €15 in season. Go before 08:00 for the light and the shade.
itinerary.afternoon: Local bus to Perast for about €2, then the boat to Our Lady of the Rocks, an island church built on sunken ships.
itinerary.evening: Last night: grilled squid by the harbour and the hostel's rooftop.

itinerary.title: Budva beach, then home
itinerary.morning: Bus to Budva in 40 minutes for a last swim at the old town beach.
itinerary.afternoon: Bus to Tivat airport in 30 minutes, or two hours to Dubrovnik for more flights.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hostel in Baščaršija
accommodationStrategy.description: Pick one inside the bazaar quarter with a kitchen and a common room; most run the free walking tour and evening outings.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hostel in the old town of Mostar
accommodationStrategy.description: Family-run hostels here sell the Blagaj and Kravica day and often include breakfast.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hostel inside Kotor's walls
accommodationStrategy.description: Two well-known hostels sit inside the walls, so the fortress climb starts at your door.

logistics.connectivity: Montenegro and Bosnia are outside EU roaming; buy a local prepaid SIM for about €5 or use hostel wifi.
logistics.weather: Mostar is one of the hottest towns in Europe in July; carry water on the minibus day.
logistics.bookingWindows: The Sarajevo to Mostar train has no seat reservations; arrive 20 minutes early in summer.
logistics.money: Bosnia uses the convertible mark (BAM, about €0.51); Montenegro uses the euro. Small places are cash only.
logistics.transportRules: Buses charge about €1 to €2 for each bag in the hold; keep coins.
logistics.health: Tap water is safe in all three towns.
logistics.gettingThere: Fly into Sarajevo and out of Tivat or Dubrovnik to avoid doubling back.

proTips: Take the Sarajevo to Mostar train, not the bus: same price, half the bends and the canyon views.
Climb Kotor's walls before 08:00; the ticket booth opens later and the steps are in shade.
Pay for Blagaj and Kravica through the hostel; the shared minibus is cheaper than two buses and a taxi.

packingNotes: A padlock for the hostel lockers
A shawl or long sleeves for the mosques
whatCouldGoWrong: The Mostar train can be replaced by a bus at short notice; check the station board the day before.
The border at Debeli Brijeg can add an hour on summer weekends.
